name: Roman Coin
description: A small silver denarius, the everyday currency of the Roman world — used to buy bread, pay soldiers, and settle debts across the empire.
facts: A legionary earned roughly 225 denarii a year under Augustus.
Coins carried the emperor's portrait, making them a tool of propaganda.
Denarius comes from the Latin for 'containing ten', its original value in bronze asses.

name: Roman Helmet
description: A legionary's galea, built to deflect downward sword blows with its broad neck-guard and reinforced brow band.
facts: Cheek guards were hinged so the helmet could be removed quickly.
A horsehair crest often marked rank rather than decoration alone.
Padded liners protected against the weight of the metal shell.

name: Roman Vase
description: An amphora used to transport wine, olive oil, and fish sauce across the Mediterranean by ship — the shipping container of the ancient world.
facts: The pointed base let amphorae be stacked upright in wet sand for stability.
Merchants stamped the clay with a maker's mark before firing.
Wrecked amphorae are one of the main ways archaeologists trace ancient trade routes.

name: Temple Relief
description: A carved marble fragment from a temple frieze, once brightly painted, showing scenes honouring a Roman deity.
facts: Temple exteriors were originally painted in vivid colour, not bare white marble.
Reliefs like this often depicted processions, sacrifices, or myths.
Temples served as both religious sites and treasuries for the city.
